Its statement was read here: for finite transition-table machines over binary words, with read-only input heads, binary work tapes, one coin bit per step and space at most $c\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil$ on every coin tape, the classes L, RL (polynomial clock, $\ge1/2$ versus $0$) and BPL ($\ge2/3$ versus $\le1/3$) satisfy L = RL and RL = BPL. That is the headline. Not rebuilt here. The paper's quantitative approximation ($2^{-q}$ accuracy in space $O(\log n+q)$) and its explicit compiler are not part of the Comparator statement. The paper concerns polynomial-time randomized logspace; it does not claim that randomized logspace machines without a time bound are derandomized.

Its statements were read here: for a fixed deterministic machine with one writable tape and head plus finitely many read-only heads, whose initial symbols are computable in polylogarithmic space, a multitape machine given $x$ and a binary cap $T\ge2$ outputs the finite-control state and halting flag at time $T$ within $cT^{2/5}(\log(T+2))^e$ work bits; a capless version does the same at a halting time $t$ within $c(t+2)^{2/5}$ times a polylog. That gives $O(T^{1/2-\delta})$ for every $\delta<1/10$, the headline. Not rebuilt here. The bound carries polylogarithmic factors, the simulation is not time-efficient, and the multitape exponent is not improved.
